data.title: Israel Inflation Jumps, But Falls Short Of Forecasts
data.description:
Israel’s monthly inflation rate accelerated to 0.7% in the latest reading, more than double the previous 0.3%. The 0.4 percentage point rise, a roughly 133% increase, marks a clear uptick in price momentum compared with the prior month.

However, the figure undershot analysts’ 0.9% estimate, signaling that inflation pressures are rising but slightly less intense than markets expected. Local equities are likely to react with mixed sentiment, as higher inflation supports near-term caution for rate-sensitive banks and real estate while the downside surprise may temper expectations for aggressive monetary tightening, influencing longer-term policy pricing.

data.description:

The actual print matched analyst estimates at 0.6%, limiting surprise-driven volatility but reinforcing expectations of persistent inflation in the euro area. Spanish equities are likely to see pressure in rate-sensitive sectors such as banks and real estate, as investors reassess monetary policy trajectories. Consumer-facing stocks may experience short-term sentiment swings as higher prices squeeze household purchasing power.

data.title: Pennpetro pivots from Ukrainian oil to Canadian biofuels with ICENERGY reverse takeover plan
data.description:
Pennpetro Energy Plc ( (GB:PPP) ) has provided an announcement.

Pennpetro Energy has abandoned its planned Ukrainian oil and gas acquisition strategy, citing the challenges of due diligence, valuation and funding amid the ongoing conflict, and will instead pursue a reverse takeover of Indigenous Canadian Energy Holdings Inc. The board says the Ukrainian opportunity will continue to be advanced by a separate private vehicle, while Pennpetro seeks to realign its portfolio and provide clarity to shareholders ahead of its AGM.

ICENERGY is a Canadian transition energy business that converts low-quality waste wood fibre into steam-enhanced black pellets, a coal replacement for residential and industrial heat and power, and is developing biochemical by-products. With first production and revenue expected from a U.S. facility in October 2026 and further plants planned in Canada, a successful reverse takeover would shift Pennpetro toward biofuels and could strengthen its positioning in renewable infrastructure markets, subject to regulatory, funding and shareholder approvals.

data.title: Cohort Plc Amends Director LTIP Figures After Growth Beats Targets
data.description:

Cohort plc has corrected previously reported figures for Finance Director Simon Walther’s long‑term incentive plan (LTIP) share vesting, confirming that 39,635 shares vested and 18,679 were sold to meet tax and National Insurance liabilities. The amendment leaves all other details unchanged and forms part of a broader disclosure on the vesting and post‑vesting holding of LTIP awards for Chief Executive Andrew Thomis and Walther.

Under the 2023 LTIP, both executives received vested shares at nil cost on 29 August 2026, with portions sold on 1 September at £11.6176 per share to cover statutory charges, and the remaining shares locked into a two‑year holding period in a custodian nominee account. The awards were fully earned after Cohort significantly exceeded its three‑year organic and total compound annual growth rate targets, reinforcing the alignment of executive rewards with strong business performance and giving investors clearer visibility on director shareholdings.

data.title: Nestmedic’s PregnaOne 510(k) Moves Into Substantive FDA Review
data.description:

Nestmedic has moved to a new phase in its U.S. regulatory push, as the Food and Drug Administration has formally accepted its 510(k) submission for the PregnaOne system and assigned a Lead Reviewer under number K263053. The file is now under substantive review in the Office of Health Technology 3B, the unit responsible for obstetrics and reproductive health devices, marking a key milestone but not yet implying marketing approval.

The company notes that FDA may request further data or clarifications during a possible Substantive Interaction and expects the next major contact with the regulator in about 45 days, in line with typical timelines. Management views this progress in the 510(k) process as an important step in executing its strategy to introduce PregnaOne to the U.S. market, a priority growth avenue for the firm, and will report subsequent significant regulatory developments as required.
